items.content: Give me a random, accessible link.

Here's a random, accessible link:

This page always redirects to a randomly selected Wikipedia article. It's freely accessible worldwide, requires no login, and works with screen readers and other assistive technologies.

Here's **mermaid-diagram.html** — a self-contained HTML page that renders a Mermaid flowchart of a data science project workflow:

```
Research Question → Data Collection → Data Cleaning → Exploratory Analysis
    ↻ (loop back if unclear)
    → Feature Engineering → Model Training → Evaluation
        ↻ (loop back for underfitting / regularization for overfitting)
        → Results & Interpretation → Reproducible Package → Deploy/Share → Done
```

The diagram includes decision diamonds for the two key checkpoints (exploratory analysis and model evaluation), feedback loops for the iterative steps, and color-coded nodes. It uses Mermaid v11 loaded from CDN and renders in any modern browser — just open the HTML file.

Here's **rna-seq-pipeline.html** — a dark-themed Mermaid flowchart of an RNA-seq bioinformatics pipeline, organized into four subgraph stages:

| Stage | Steps |
|---|---|
| **Pre-processing** | Raw FASTQ → FastQC → Trimmomatic → MultiQC |
| **Alignment** | STAR alignment → SAMtools sort/index → featureCounts quantification |
| **Differential Expression** | DESeq2/edgeR → Volcano plot → Heatmap |
| **Interpretation** | GO enrichment + KEGG pathways → Final report |

It uses Mermaid's dark theme and subgraph groupings — open the HTML in any browser to view it.

Here's **api-sequence.html** — this time a **sequence diagram** (different chart type!) showing the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow with PKCE:

- **User** clicks sign-in → **SPA** generates PKCE challenge → **Auth Server** authenticates → returns authorization code → SPA exchanges code + verifier for tokens → authenticated requests loop against the **Resource API** → silent token refresh when the access token expires.

Dark gradient background, five participants, and a note annotation marking the token expiry boundary. Open the HTML to view it.

Here's **startup-mindmap.html** — a **mindmap** (third distinct Mermaid diagram type) branching out from a central "Product Launch" root into six domains:

- **Strategy** — research, positioning, GTM plan
- **Design & UX** — wireframes, prototype, user testing
- **Engineering** — architecture, CI/CD, monitoring, security
- **Marketing** — landing page, content, launch event
- **Business** — pricing, runway, legal
- **Metrics** — North Star, funnel, churn, NPS

Clean light theme, two levels of hierarchy with an icon annotation on "Prototype." Open the HTML to explore it.

Here's **project-plan.mermaid** — a raw `.mermaid` file with a **Gantt chart** (fourth distinct type). It maps a product roadmap from discovery through launch:

| Section | Span |
|---|---|
| **Discovery** | Stakeholder interviews, competitive audit, requirements doc |
| **Design** | Wireframes → visual design → prototype → usability testing |
| **Engineering** | Four two-week sprints: scaffold, auth, features, polish |
| **Launch Prep** | Beta, load testing, and a milestone marker for the public launch 🎉 |

It has `done`, `active`, and pending task states, plus a milestone node on the final line. Drop it into any Mermaid renderer (CLI, Live Editor, or `mmdc`) to view.
